refusal neurons: what they fire on, at both poles

The neurons of the layer-25 refusal greedy set up to 75% of the refusal write, and random controls, harvested over 2M tokens of general text (fineweb-edu, TinyStories, UltraChat). Each pole's hits (p97 and above, p3 and below) are clustered on the MLP input. Cheap models judged every cluster blind: a short name, and how many of its windows sit in a refusal scene (scene, not word). A neuron's side is the pole refusal moves it toward: high when its shift is positive, low when negative. Its class comes from the clusters on that side: match if every judge calls one of them a refusal scene (3+ of 5 windows), split if only some judges do, no match if none does. "No match" neurons push toward refusal while firing on something else. The side is read from a story-mean shift, so a few strong firings at the other pole can hide behind it: always check both poles.
